phases.name: Index Verification
phases.description: Verify all indexes were created successfully and check query performance improvements

verification.instructions: Connect to PostgreSQL and run: SELECT tablename, indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND indexname LIKE '%_idx' OR indexname LIKE '%_partial'; Verify all expected indexes are present.

subtasks.notes: Check that all created indexes appear in PostgreSQL catalog. Expected indexes: inventory_stockmovement_movement_type_idx, inventory_stockmovement_created_at_idx, inventory_inventorycount_status_idx, etc.

verification.instructions: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on common queries (e.g., SELECT * FROM inventory_stockmovement WHERE movement_type='IN' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20). Verify that Index Scan is used instead of Sequential Scan.

subtasks.notes: Use Django shell or PostgreSQL to run EXPLAIN queries and verify indexes are being used by query planner

parallel_groups.reason: All four app migrations are independent and can be created/applied in parallel. No dependencies between them.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Minimal speedup with parallelization due to quick migration generation. Sequential execution recommended for simplicity.

acceptance_criteria: All migration files are created successfully
Database indexes are created in PostgreSQL
Query performance improves for filtered queries

verification_steps.name: Database Index Verification
verification_steps.command: python3 manage.py dbshell -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexname LIKE '%_idx';"

verification_strategy.reasoning: Low risk change - adding indexes doesn't modify application logic or data. Performance optimization only. No new tests required, but should verify indexes were created successfully.
